The instant appeal has been filed against the judgment dated 22/08/2014 passed by 15th Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur in S.T. No. 88/2013, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for ten years along with fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 376(2)(I) of IPC and sentenced to undergo Life imprisonment along with a fine of Rs.10,000/- and Section 6 of the POCSO Act with default stipulations.

2. The brief facts necessary for proper adjudication of the case are that on 22/09/2013 at about 9:15 p.m., PW-1 Smt. Savitri Bai, along with her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18187 2 CRA-3030-2014 husband Gulab Singh and their daughter (prosecutrix), reached Police Station Sihora, District Jabalpur, and lodged an oral complaint.
She stated that at about 2:00 p.m. on the same day, the appellant (Jaggu) came to her house and, by offering a toffee, enticed the prosecutrix and attempted to take her away.
Upon being questioned, the appellant informed her that he was taking the child to the nearby society and would return shortly.
When the appellant and the prosecutrix did not return within a reasonable time, her husband went in search of the child and later returned with her.
The prosecutrix's clothes were found smeared with mud and dung.
While bathing the child, her husband noticed that she was not permitting anyone to touch her waist and complained of pain.

Later, when both parents questioned her about the pain, she disclosed that the Jag Mohan @ Jaggu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156906243/
1 appellant had taken her to the house of Jagdish, which was used for keeping cattle, where he undressed her and committed rape.

Statements of mother, father, and other family members of the prosecutrix were recorded under Section 161 of Code of Criminal Procedure and the statements of the parents were also recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate.
The prosecutrix and the accused were medically examined, relevant articles were seized, the accused was arrested and a spot map was prepared.

5. On 23/10/2013, the learned trial Court framed charges against the accused under Sections 363,
366 and 376(2)(I) of the IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The accused denied the charges and wished to face trial.

6. In order to substantiate its case, the prosecution examined total seven witnesses (PW-1 to PW-7)
and exhibited documents marked as Ex. P- 1 to P-20.
The accused/appellant did not examine any witness nor produce any document in support of his defence.

In his statement recorded under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused asserted that he is innocent, has not committed any offence, and has been falsely implicated due to previous enmity.

7. Learned trial Court, after appreciating the material available on record, concluded that the appellant had committed offences punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376(2)(I) of the IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
Accordingly, by judgment dated 22/08/2014, the Court sentenced him to undergo life imprisonment and imposed a total fine of Rs. 15,000/-.

8. Aggrieved by the impugned judgment, the appellant has preferred NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18187 4 CRA-3030-2014 the present appeal on the grounds that he is innocent,
has not committed any offence, and has been falsely implicated due to previous enmity.
It is further contended that neither the MLC nor the FSL report conclusively establishes that the alleged offence was committed by the appellant.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that there existed prior enmity between the complainant and the accused, and on account of such enmity, the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that MLC does not disclose any internal or external injury on the person of the prosecutrix, and her hymen was found to be intact.

The doctor did not Jag Mohan @ Jaggu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156906243/
2 give any definite opinion regarding commission of rape or attempt thereof.

It is further submitted that the seized articles were sent for chemical examination to the State Forensic Science Laboratory,
Sagar and as per FSL Report (Ex. P-19), no male sperm was detected in Article 'A', which is the swab sample of the prosecutrix.
10.
Learned counsel also pointed out that PW-3 (prosecutrix), in her cross-examination, admitted that the appellant had not committed anything with her.
Additionally, it is argued that there are material omissions and contradictions in the statements of PW-1 and PW-2, which create doubt in the prosecution case.
Thus, upon overall consideration of the evidence on record, it is contended that there is no sufficient material to hold the appellant guilty of the alleged offences.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State contended that the learned trial Court, after proper appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence on record and after considering the defence taken by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18187 5 CRA-3030-2014 the appellant, has rightly held the appellant guilty of the alleged offences.
In the MLC, the doctor found reddish abrasion marks on the private parts of the prosecutrix.
At the time of being bathed by her father, the prosecutrix complained of pain in the lower waist region.
PW-1 and PW-2, who are the parents of the prosecutrix, have duly supported the prosecution case as narrated by the prosecutrix.
PW-3 (prosecutrix)

, in her deposition before the trial Court, after the Court satisfied itself regarding her competency, stated that the accused had taken her away by offering a toffee, brought her to the place of occurrence, threw her on the floor, undressed her, and committed rape.
She further deposed that when she cried due to pain, the accused sent her back home.
Her clothes were found smeared with mud and dung.

Dr.S.Palod (PW-4), in her examination-in-chief before the trial Court, stated that during the external examination she found reddish abrasion marks accompanied by pain around the private parts of the prosecutrix.
12. It is further submitted that no discharge was found on the private parts of the prosecutrix.
In cross-examination, the doctor stated, in response to a suggestion, that such reddish abrasion marks could possibly occur if the prosecutrix had fallen on an uneven surface or due to itching.

However,
the doctor did not give any opinion that the prosecutrix was suffering from any itching or similar condition affecting her private parts.
It is therefore submitted that the judgment passed by the learned trial Court is well- reasoned and speaking, does not suffer from any infirmity, and does not warrant interference.
Accordingly, dismissal of the appeal is prayed for.

13. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18187 6 CRA-3030-2014 record.
14. The sole question arises for our consideration is whether the learned trial Court has committed any illegality or perversity in passing the impugned judgment.
15. Perusal of record clearly reveals that FIR (Ex. P-9) was lodged by PW-1, Smt. Savitri Bai.

The contents mentioned in the FIR, as well as the statements of PW-1 and PW-2 recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and their statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate, remained consistent with their depositions before the Court.

The prosecutrix, a four-year-old child, narrated Jag Mohan @ Jaggu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156906243/
3 the incident to her parents in the same manner as alleged in the FIR, and she reiterated the same facts in her deposition before the trial Court.

sentences.text: The consistency in the depositions of PW-1, PW-2, and PW-3 was not seriously challenged by the appellant during cross- examination.
16. Dr. PW-4, Dr. S.Padot, a pediatrician, conducted the medical examination of the prosecutrix and prepared the MLC (Ex. P-7).
In the MLC, she did not find any internal or external injury; the hymen was found intact.
However, she observed a reddish abrasion injury on the private parts of the prosecutrix.
In paragraph 2 of her examination-in-chief before the Court, she specifically admitted the presence of such reddish abrasion marks on the private part of the child.
17. PW-5, Dr. Rajiv Singhai, medically examined the accused and prepared the medical examination report (Ex. P-8).
At the time of examination he found the appellant capable of performing sexual intercourse.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18187 7 CRA-3030-2014
During the medical examination, the underwear of the accused was seized and a slide was prepared.
As per the FSL report, human sperm was detected on the slide prepared from the seized underwear.
18. As per counsel for the appellant the appellant has been falsely implicated on account of previous enmity.

19. It is a well-settled principle that previous enmity is a double- edged weapon: one edge may furnish a motive for the accused to commit the offence, while the other may provide a ground for false implication.
Therefore, while considering such a defence of prior enmity, the Court is required to exercise due caution and evaluate the same carefully in light of the material available on record.
20. In the present case, PW-1 and PW-2, in their depositions before the trial Court, denied the suggestion put to them in cross-examination that there was any previous enmity between the parties.
Moreover, if there had been any prior enmity, there would have been no occasion for PW-1 to permit the accused to take her daughter along with him.
This circumstance further weakens the defence plea of false implication on account of previous enmity.
21. In his defence, the appellant has not specified the nature of the alleged previous enmity.
A mere assertion that he has been falsely implicated due to prior enmity is not sufficient.
It was incumbent upon the appellant to substantiate the existence and nature of such enmity between him and the complainant.

22. PW-3 (prosecutrix) has deposed that when the accused took her NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18187 8 CRA-3030-2014 from her house, her mother was present and had permitted her to accompany him.
Thereafter, the accused took her to the place of occurrence and committed the offence.
23. In view of these circumstances, the plea of false implication on account of previous enmity does not inspire confidence and stands negatived.

sentences.text: As per the testimony of PW-3, the appellant undressed her and committed rape.
The MLC indicates that the doctor found reddish abrasion injuries around the private parts of the prosecutrix and also noted that there was no discharge.
In such circumstances, the absence of spermatozoa on the swab/slide taken from the private parts of the prosecutrix cannot by itself negate the prosecution case.
The non-detection of human sperm is not conclusive proof that the offence was not committed.

25. Upon an overall consideration of the documentary as well as oral evidence available on record,
we are of the view that the learned trial court, after proper appreciation of the material placed before it has recorded a well- reasoned and speaking judgment.
26. We do not find any substantial merit in the grounds or arguments advanced by the appellant so as to warrant interference with the impugned judgment, which is reasoned and in accordance with law.
27. Accordingly, the appeal filed by the appellant is hereby dismissed.
